title: [A] Locate the failure window in database-plus-broker workflows
brief: An order API commits SQL state and publishes an event to a broker. Customers report accepted orders missing from shipping; a recent retry change also caused duplicate shipment requests. Locate concrete failure windows and propose a reliable handoff. Do not assume a distributed transaction exists. Start by clarifying the required guarantees.

clarifications.question: Can the SQL schema change?
clarifications.answer: Yes. Orders and a new local table may participate in the same database transaction.

clarifications.question: What does shipping control?
clarifications.answer: A separate SQL store for shipment requests; its handlers can use local transactions and unique constraints.

clarifications.question: What workload and freshness are required?
clarifications.answer: 500orders/s peak;99% of accepted orders should reach shipping within30seconds during healthy operation. Outages can be caught up without silently losing accepted orders.

hints: Draw the exact point between the first durable effect and the second.
Distinguish repeating publication from repeating a committed shipment request.
State what the recovery checkpoint proves.
changes: The relay stops for40minutes while the API remains healthy.
A consumer receives the same event ID with a different payload.
referenceSolution: Put order and event intent in one SQL transaction; relay committed intents with stable event IDs and per-order ordering where required. Accept that relay publication can repeat after a crash. At shipping, commit a unique processed-event marker with creation of the shipment request. Preserve original results for duplicates and reject conflicting payload identities. Monitor oldest outstanding age, backlog, relay throughput, poison schemas and reconciliation. At500/s for2,400seconds the backlog is1.2million events before new traffic; catch-up capacity must exceed arrivals. Do not promise the eventual physical shipment or external carrier action belongs to the SQL transaction. A supported distributed transaction is an alternative only with participant support and accepted availability costs.
debrief: Replay each proposed crash point. Award feedback only for actual candidate evidence: local atomic boundary, duplicate-safe receiver, retention/recovery, units, and an explicit external-effect limit. A correct pattern name without its failure trace is weak evidence.
